h1: Top 10 Most Expensive Chinese Cars Ever Built

contentBlocks.text: Forget everything you think you know about Chinese cars.

For years, the Western world looked down on the Chinese domestic market as a breeding ground for cheap, plastic commuter appliances and shameless, copycat design clones. But while we were sleeping, something massive shifted in the global balance of horsepower. Today, China isn’t just catching up to Western engineering; they are aggressively pricing themselves into a stratosphere once reserved exclusively for Maranello, Stuttgart, and Goodwood.

We’re not talking about your everyday grocery-getters here. We’re talking about wild quad-motor hypercars that can literally dance, V12-powered state limos wrapped in political secrecy, and absolute leviathans built to survive the apocalypse. To show you just how crazy things have gotten, we tracked down the prices and dug into the specs.
These are the 10 most expensive Chinese cars ever built—and they’re not asking for permission.
1. Hongqi S9 (~$1.49 Million)
2. Nio EP9 (~$1.48 Million)
3. Hongqi Guoli (~$1.45 Million)
4. ArcFox GT (~$1.2 Million)
6. Dongfeng Mengshi M-Hunter ($521,000+)
7. BYD Yangwang U9 (~$253,000)
8. GAC Aion Hyper SSR (~$231,000)
10. BYD Yangwang U8 (~$152,000)
1Hongqi S9
Estimated Price: $1,490,000
The Verdict: A 1,400-hp hybrid missile built right in Ferrari’s backyard to prove a point.

For a long time, Hongqi was mostly known for the big, black sedans used by Chinese government officials. Most people outside of China didn't really know the brand, and nobody associated it with high-performance cars.

The S9 changed that. To build this car, Hongqi set up a base in Italy’s Motor Valley, right near famous names like Ferrari and Pagani. They even hired Walter de Silva, the designer who did the Audi R8, to handle the styling. The result is a carbon-fiber supercar that looks nothing like the brand’s traditional models.

Under the skin, the S9 uses a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 engine paired with three electric motors. This setup produces a ridiculous 1,400 horsepower. Hongqi claims the car can go from 0 to 100 km/h in a blistering 1.9 seconds and top out at over 248 mph.

Hongqi is only making 99 units of the S9, and each one costs around 10 million yuan. The car isn't meant to be a big seller. Instead, this halo car exists to show European carmakers that China has the technology and resources to compete in the supercar market.
2Nio EP9
Estimated Price: $1,480,000
The Verdict: A record-shattering electric track monster that introduced the world to Chinese EV performance by humbling the Nürburgring.

Nio built the EP9 to prove that a Chinese startup could compete with the world's top performance cars. Back in 2016, before they were known for SUVs and battery swapping, they released this car to show they were a serious player. It managed a lap time of 6:45.90 at the Nürburgring, which was actually faster than many famous European hypercars at that time.

The way it is built is fairly straightforward but very powerful. There are four separate motors, one for each wheel, and each has its own gearbox. This setup delivers 1,360 horsepower. The car can reach 200 km/h in 7.1 seconds and pulls 3.3 Gs in the corners—which is enough lateral force to give your neck a serious workout.

Nio only made a handful of these. They built the first six for their main investors and then offered a few more to others. Because they are so rare, a unit kept by the factory recently sold for its original price of $1.48 million. The EP9 was never meant for normal driving; it was really just an expensive way to demonstrate that electric cars could be incredibly fast.
3Hongqi Guoli
Estimated Price: $1,450,000
The Verdict: A massive, V8-powered rolling fortress built for billionaires who want the ultimate Chinese political status symbol.

If the Hongqi S9 is China trying to beat Italy at its own game, the Guoli is Hongqi doing what it does best: building imposing, old-money state limousines. Known to hardcore car geeks as the second-generation L5, this is the crown jewel of the brand's ultra-luxury "Golden Sunflower" lineup. It is designed to be the Chinese equivalent of a Rolls-Royce Phantom, but with a level of domestic political weight that no British luxury brand could ever hope to replicate.

The styling is a masterclass in nostalgic intimidation. At first glance, it keeps the iconic retro round headlights and the massive vertical chrome grille inspired by the classic CA770 state limos that carried party leaders decades ago. But look a little closer and the obsessive details stand out—like the red-flag hood ornament that is tilted at exactly 23.5 degrees to perfectly match the axial tilt of the Earth.

Under the skin, Hongqi ditched the old naturally aspirated V12 from the previous generation, swapping it out for a modern 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 producing 388 horsepower. Now, this thing weighs a staggering 3.1 tons, so it isn’t winning any drag races—0 to 100 km/h takes nearly 8 seconds—but speed is completely missing the point here.

The interior is an absolute sanctuary of handcrafted leather, jade accents, and executive rear thrones with full massage functions. Buying a Guoli isn't about flashing new money; it’s the ultimate flex to show you’ve reached the absolute highest tier of social and political standing in China.
4ArcFox GT
Estimated Price: $1,200,000
The Verdict: A track-focused all-electric hypercar that tried to give Beijing’s EV industry its own bleeding-edge halo car.

If you have never heard of ArcFox, that is because they are the high-end electric brand under BAIC, a state-owned company that usually makes basic commuter cars and off-road vehicles. In 2019, they decided to try something different. They went to Spain and partnered with Campos Racing, a team known for their work in Formula E, to develop the ArcFox GT for the Geneva Motor Show.

The goal was to create a race car that was legal to drive on public roads rather than a luxury car. It features a low carbon-fiber body and uses four electric motors, with two in the front and two in the back. Together, these motors produce 1,020 horsepower and 1,327 lb-ft of torque. Because it is electric, all that power is instantly available, allowing the car to go from 0 to 100 km/h in 2.5 seconds.

To make it functional on a track, the car includes active aerodynamics, carbon-ceramic brakes, and a stiff racing suspension that prioritizes grip over a smooth ride. It is essentially a race car with a license plate. Even with its high price, the ArcFox GT was not meant to be a big seller. It was built to prove that a company known for making ordinary family cars has the engineering ability to create a high-performance exotic.
5Hongqi L5
Estimated Price: $760,000
The Verdict: The legendary, V12-powered Chinese retro limousine that first brought state-level luxury to the public market.

Long before the Guoli came out, the Hongqi L5 was the most prestigious car in China. When it launched around 2014, it cost 5 million yuan, which made it the most expensive car built in China for about a decade. The design was a tribute to the old CA770 limousines that Chinese leaders used to use in Beijing.

The engine was one of the most interesting parts of the original L5. It featured a 6.0-liter V12, though later versions switched to a V8. It produced 402 horsepower, which was not meant for racing but provided a very smooth ride. The car is massive, weighing more than three tons, and is easily recognized by its big round headlights and wide chrome grille.

Inside, the car uses traditional Chinese details instead of modern materials like carbon fiber. It features hand-carved wood, lacquer panels, and even jade on the door handles. Buying one was not just about having the money. Hongqi actually performed background checks on potential buyers to make sure they had the right social standing before they would agree to sell them the car.
6Dongfeng Mengshi M-Hunter
Estimated Price: $521,000+
The Verdict: An unhinged, carbon-fiber electric exoskeleton built to conquer sand dunes and humiliate conventional off-roaders.

People usually think the high-end car market in China is only about fast sports cars or quiet luxury sedans, but Dongfeng is challenging that idea with the Mengshi M-Hunter. Mengshi, which means Warrior, started as a military vehicle division within Dongfeng before it became a luxury brand for civilians. With the M-Hunter, they have created something that looks like a Dakar racing buggy, featuring an open roll cage and a price tag in the millions of yuan.

The vehicle does not look like a standard SUV. It has a rugged design that looks like it belongs in a sci-fi film. There are no traditional doors or windshields. Instead, it uses a steel tube frame and a large carbon fiber hood. It sits on huge off-road tires and includes a system that lets the driver adjust tire pressure from inside the cabin, which helps when driving through deep sand or over rocks.

Dongfeng has not released all the specific performance details yet, but the M-Hunter is built on their specialized off-road platform. It uses multiple electric motors and produces a significant amount of torque. It is available as either a pure electric vehicle or a range-extended version. This is a niche vehicle built in small numbers for wealthy buyers who want a serious off-road machine that uses modern technology.
7BYD Yangwang U9
Estimated Price: $253,000
The Verdict: A heavy, quad-motor tech showcase that proves the world's biggest EV maker can build a track-ready hypercar that literally jumps.

The Yangwang U9 is a heavy, four-motor electric supercar that BYD built to prove they can make high-performance cars, not just daily commuters. Even though it costs 1.8 million yuan—making it the most affordable entry on this list—it is still a high-end, low-volume model designed to show off the company's technical abilities.

The car uses the e4 platform, which has four separate electric motors, one for each wheel. Together, these motors produce 1,287 horsepower and 1,240 lb-ft of torque. Because it carries a large 80 kWh battery, the car weighs almost 2.5 tons. However, the instant power from the electric motors still lets it hit 100 km/h in 2.36 seconds, which is on par with many gas-powered hypercars.

One of the most talked-about features is the DiSus-X active suspension system. This technology adjusts the suspension at each corner in milliseconds, keeping the car flat during turns. It is advanced enough to let the car drive on three wheels if a tire blows out or even jump off the ground from a standstill. BYD did not build this car for high sales figures. It exists mainly to show that the company has the engineering skills to compete with famous European brands.
8GAC Aion Hyper SSR
Estimated Price: $231,000
The Verdict: China’s first mass-produced electric supercar that brings sub-two-second acceleration down to an earth-bound price tag.

For a long time, GAC Aion was mainly known for making practical electric cars and taxis. With the Hyper SSR, they launched a luxury brand called Hyptec to move into the performance market. What makes this car different from many other high-end concepts is that it is actually available for people to buy right now.

The top-of-the-line Ultimate Track Edition costs 1.686 million yuan. It features a body made entirely of carbon fiber and uses three electric motors to produce 1,224 horsepower. Because electric motors provide instant power, it can go from 0 to 100 km/h in 1.9 seconds. This speed puts it in the same league as much more expensive European hypercars.

The car also includes automatic butterfly doors, carbon-ceramic brakes, and a rear wing that adjusts to help with handling during fast turns. The Hyper SSR is not intended to be a common car for daily commuting. Instead, it is a way for the company to show they can build an exotic car that competes with famous performance brands at a much lower cost.
9Maextro S800
Estimated Price: $200,000+
The Verdict: A massive, tech-loaded ultra-luxury flagship designed to beat Maybach at its own game by combining old-money presence with high-end tech.

Huawei is doing more than just competing with Apple in the phone market. The Maextro S800 shows they have big plans for cars as well. This brand is a partnership between Huawei and JAC Motors, and it is built specifically for the ultra-luxury market. Instead of going after standard luxury cars from Mercedes or BMW, they are targeting high-end models like the Maybach S-Class or the Rolls-Royce Ghost.

The car is very large, measuring nearly 5.5 meters in length. It stands out with its two-tone paint, a vertical grille with a starry pattern, and custom wheels. Even though it looks traditional, it has modern features like a LiDAR sensor on the roof and a smooth, aerodynamic shape.

Technically, the S800 uses Huawei’s driving software and an active suspension system. It is an electric car, but the focus is on the ride quality rather than just the horsepower. The suspension is designed to stay very smooth so passengers do not feel bumps in the road. Inside, the rear cabin looks like a first-class lounge, featuring a starry ceiling, individual seats, and privacy tech for people who need to work. The S800 seems to be making the argument that luxury in the future will be defined more by smart technology than by traditional heritage.
10BYD Yangwang U8
Estimated Price: $152,000
The Verdict: A 1,200-hp, tech-heavy luxury SUV that can literally float on water and spin on a dime to prove BYD can build the ultimate go-anywhere status symbol.

Most people know BYD for making affordable electric cars and family SUVs. But with the Yangwang U8, they have built a massive luxury off-roader meant to compete with famous models like the Range Rover or the Mercedes G-Wagon. It is a huge vehicle with a boxy shape, but the most interesting part is the technology under the hood.

The car uses four electric motors, one for each wheel, and a 2.0-liter engine that acts as a range extender. Together, they produce nearly 1,200 horsepower. Even though it weighs 3.5 tons, the SUV can go from 0 to 100 km/h in 3.6 seconds, which is as fast as many sports cars.

Because the wheels can spin independently, the car can do a tank turn and spin in a circle on the spot. It also has a hydraulic system that allows it to drive on three wheels if a tire fails. If it ends up in deep water, it can actually float, seal the cabin, and use its wheels to paddle back to land at a slow speed.

The inside is very different from the rugged exterior, featuring leather seats, a high-end sound system, and a large curved screen. The U8 is really a way for BYD to show that they can pack more technology into a car than almost any other luxury car company.
Final Thoughts

For a long time, the ultra-luxury car market was basically a private club for European and British brands. If you wanted a car that cost hundreds of thousands or even millions of dollars, your choices were limited to high-end Italian, German, or British names.
This list of ten cars shows that the traditional manufacturers now have some serious competition.

China’s car industry has moved past just making affordable electric cars and family SUVs. They are now building high-end performance cars like the four-motor Yangwang U9, the Nio EP9, and the carbon-fiber Mengshi M-Hunter. At the same time, brands like Hongqi and Huawei are showing that luxury can be defined by software and status, not just traditional materials like leather and wood.

These vehicles aren't actually meant to sell in huge numbers. They are built to show off what these companies are capable of. They are meant to prove that China has the technology and the money to build world-class exotic cars.
